newsitem.title: USA: Employee Solutions stock slumps on rumors.
newsitem.headline: Employee Solutions stock slumps on rumors.

text.p: Employee Solutions Inc. lost about half of its market value, or over $300 million, on Thursday on fears the provider of temporary workers' delayed fourth-quarter earnings may not live up to expectations.

The stock was further punished by rumors that its chairman and chief executive, Marvin Brody, has been selling unregistered shares of the company in Europe, which caused panic selling among investors.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Brody denied the stock sale rumor. "That is not true, no selling whatsoever," he said. "That rumor is false."

Shares of the Phoenix, Ariz.-based company fell $4.50 to $15.375 on Nasdaq during normal trading hours. However, after the company announced it was delaying indefinitely the release of its fourth-quarter financial results, the stock fell another $5.375 to $10 in after hours trading.
The stock was the third most heavily traded on Nasdaq with 11.6 million shares changing hands. The company had about 33 million shares outstanding at the end of its third quarter.
Employee Solutions declined to give a reason for the delay but a spokeswoman said the company is working to reschedule the release as soon as possible.
One source close to the company said the delay was due to difficulties in collating results because Employee Solutions made six or seven acquisitions during the fiscal year.
Earlier, analysts said the sell-off was due to nervousness about the company's fourth-quarter earnings.
"There is a lot of nervousness about the company's earnings release," said Warren Albergotti, an analyst at The Volume Investor who follows the stock.
"There have been a lot of rumors that they are not going to be able to meet expectations," he said.

According to First Call, analysts expect the company to earn 14 cents a share for the fourth quarter, up from 6 cents or $250,000 in the same period last year, after accounting for a two-for-one stock split.

"I am extremely confident they will meet analysts' expectations," Albergotti said. "I believe most of the rumors have been spread by short sellers who have plagued the stock for over two years. We've never been able to find a single shred of evidence to support any of them."
Stacy Kleven, an analyst at TIS Group, said the fall in the stock was due to the rumors, coupled with the heavy short position and a large holder selling the stock at market prices Thursday.
